title: Not Genmu
text: “Well, I’ll drop by Siltvelt to see how things are going too… if I can’t settle down there, I’ll set up base at Éclair-san’s territory for a while, or maybe at Lars-chan’s village.”
“Got it, nano. Oh, and one more thing, Spear Hero.”
“What is it, I say?”
“That thing about timing things so you deal with the Spirit Tortoise problem before it happens—you don’t need to do that this loop, nano. So you can go play on Cal Mira Island for longer, nano.”
“Is that so, indeed?”
Rival had been asking me to time things so I’d unload Brionac at the designated location before the trouble started, but apparently I didn’t need to do that this loop, I say.
“Nano.”
“Hmph. Not bad, are you. By the way, what do you intend to do about the Spirit Tortoise’s country this loop? Poking at a hornet’s nest could be interesting, no?”
“That’s enough of that, nano…”
Ugh, my trauma!? Was Rafumi-chan planning to revive the Spirit Tortoise, I wonder?
“Stop it, seriously, I say! It’ll spread infamy far and wide—do you want to kill Ren’s companions, indeed!?”
“Even Rafumi isn’t that cruel. I’ve made reinforcements so they can survive.”
“So there’s a death event for Ren’s companions in the next Cal Mira Island event or something?”
“Well, more or less, nano.”
Father seemed to have judged this an event requiring caution as well.
“Not that one—I mean the Spirit Tortoise’s country.”
“Ah… well, the so-called ‘pretend villainess’ will just have to keep working hard this loop too, nano.”
“Someone you know?”
“Naofumi and the Heroes don’t need to worry about it, nano. Even if they show up, don’t engage with them, nano. Engaging just makes the damage worse, nano.”
I had no idea who they meant, but it seemed to be someone Rival knew, indeed. Was there such a person?
“Fufu… the state of that one after the peaceful end of the waves is rather amusing, no?”
“Don’t say it, nano.”
“Getting desperate and bowing deeply to us, begging us to expose their true identity—that sounds amusing too.”
“You’re a demon, nano.”

Rival and Rafumi-chan kept exchanging looks, and even Father turned to me as if to ask whether I knew anything, but I had no idea either, I say. Please stop carrying on with inside jokes! I don’t understand any of it, indeed!
“That kind of suggestive talk is really bothering me… wasn’t the Spirit Tortoise supposed to be an auspicious beast? Does it actually exist?”
“Indeed. It’s a bitter memory of us getting ahead of ourselves and doing all sorts of things, I say.”
Painful even to recall—something that Ren, Itsuki, and I went through, indeed.

“After Cal Mira Island, we got it into our heads that we’d grown strong, and treated it as a convenient boss to skip ahead to for a big equipment upgrade, so we revived it and caused a massive disaster, indeed. It’s an event that’s better left un-triggered, I say.”
“This loop, the Sword and Bow Heroes seem outside the scope of interest, but it’d be good to stay cautious, nano.”
“Right.”
“Now, about the precautions regarding the country where the Spirit Tortoise is sealed, nano—”
“Something wrong?”
“It’s an exclusionary country, and honestly, the head—well, the king—is pretty awful too, nano.”
No question it was an exclusionary country. Even from game knowledge, it was a problematic setup, indeed.
“Suited to Itsuki?”
“No mistake there, nano. But it’s better not to let him go, nano. Handle it wrong and the Spirit Tortoise revives, causing a disaster, nano.”
“Right, I sort of got that from Motoyasu-kun’s story too. Anything else?”
“If you ever go to that country, there’s a word you absolutely must never say—good to remember that too, nano.”
“Fu… indeed. If the Heroes said it, they might get executed, no?”
Rafumi-chan was laughing with a note of sarcasm, indeed.
“What is it?”

“In that country, you must never call the Spirit Tortoise ‘Genmu,’ nano. In this world, it doesn’t exist as such—well, it’s a monster name passed down through the Dragon Emperor’s knowledge, and there’s also a race called the Genmu, nano.”
At Rival’s addition, Father tilted his head slightly, indeed.
“It’s definitely a turtle connection. But is it something people actually mix up?”
“Apparently in that country, every so often, some fool comes out of nowhere, mistakes it for Genmu, and gets executed for it, nano.”

“Isn’t that odd? Mistaking it for a monster name that doesn’t even exist in this world… if it were mixing it up with the Genmu race, that’d make sense. Or is it some incognito hero? People do get summoned from other worlds after all.”
“Not a hero, nano. Not someone well-versed in archaeology either, nano. Gaelion thinks their intelligence is definitely low, nano.”
Rival answered, sounding rather exasperated, indeed.
“Ah, right, didn’t Takt’s case mean there are reincarnators around? So it’s probably someone like that mixing up the country’s name with the sealed monster’s name?”
“Correct, nano.”
“Truly foolish lot.”
“Naofumi and the others should be careful too, nano.”
“Well, I don’t think we’d normally mix it up. What I’m curious about is where Gaelion-chan even knows about Genmu from—is it from the Dragon Emperor?”
“Half right, nano. The other half is that in the world where the Spear Hero abandoned Gaelion, Genmu exists there, nano.”
“Ah, I see. Abandoned, huh… well, Motoyasu-kun did mess up pretty badly there, so.”
“That’s not messing up, I say!”
Truly outrageous, indeed. Rival, you can just stay in that other world forever, I say!
“Setting that issue aside… what comes after? Faubrey and that side—I believe Motoyasu-kun already settled things there, right?”
“Indeed. With the matter of Takt, things are already settled, I say.”
I’d already settled things with Pig King, indeed. Thanks to shipping out Takt’s pig, they were letting quite a lot slide, indeed.
“As for the rest, the troublesome ones over there can be handled with information provided by Gaelion and the others, nano.”
“Not sharing it, in terms of scope, might be an option too, no?”
“Our side has more than enough strength to deal with it, so it’s less about scope and more just a hassle, nano.”
“Is that really fine?”
“Letting them swim a bit makes them easier to hunt too, so it’s tricky, nano. Some of the Seven Star Weapons still need to be searched for, so pinpointing them is a hassle, nano.”
That had indeed been a hassle at the time. In a way, letting Takt swim and gather things himself could’ve been an option, but Takt wouldn’t be satisfied unless he suffered, I say.
“In any case, I think it’d be best for Naofumi and the others to keep tackling the waves while acting freely, nano. If there are problems, Gaelion and the others will offer advice, nano.”
“Right. We too must challenge the unknown, mustn’t we.”
“I don’t quite get the meaning of challenging the unknown, but…”
“No need to worry about it, nano—Rafumi says this too, but can you really call it living if your life comes with a strategy guide, nano?”
“Well… you could say it’s precisely because the future is unknown that people can keep moving forward.”

Quite the philosophical talk, indeed. Come to think of it, Ark and Hou-kun had said something about being able to see the future, but they’d laughed cheerfully about how low the probability was of it actually happening. They seemed to understand that even if they saw it, the future wouldn’t necessarily turn out that way. As Father’s words suggested, even seeing the future still leaves the unknown. The spirit of the spear had also said it was best not to repeat the same actions, and fate exists precisely so it can be overturned, indeed.
“Anyway, I’ve got a general idea of our course of action for now. Ren and Itsuki are both doing as they please, so—Rafumi-chan, please steer Ren in the right direction, okay?”
“Understood. If Azott makes an irreversible mistake, it becomes an enormous headache, after all. While I’m at it, I’ll follow up on that king as well.”
“That worries me tremendously, but if you’re saying you’ll take responsibility, I suppose there’s no helping it, nano.”
“Leave it to me.”
“Now I’m getting anxious…”
And so, in that sort of way, the meeting among Rival and the others came to a close, indeed.
